To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for each type combination, there are 9, 27, or 81 topological predicates (depending on the complexity of the spatial objects), and that (ii) the predicates are mutually exclusive, i.e., each spatial object has a unique topological signature.

there exist 1, 4, 16, 16, and 64 topological relationships for the type combinations complex point-complex point, complex point-complex line, complex point-comple region, complex line-complex region, and complex region-complex region.
for complex points, lines, and regions there are 1, 4, and 7 topological relationships, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the definition and classification of topological predicates and relationships for complex spatial data types and the design and implementation of an efficient algorithm for the computation of these relationships.
the definition of topological relationships between complex objects and their application to complex spatial data types.
the development of a general framework for the design, specification, and use of complex spatial data and their topological predicates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there exist exactly 16, 256, 128 topological relationships between complex points and regions, 16, 384 topological relationships between regions, 16 topological relationships between lines and regions, and 16, 896 topological relationships between points and lines.
topological relationships between complex objects can be handled in a similar way as between simple ones.
the 9-intersection based topological relationships are applicable to any combination of the introduced spatial data types and are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the complete sets of topological predicates for all type combinations of the three basic types of spatial data.

we provide an approach for the design of a large number of topological relationship predicates, which can be applied to any spatial data type and are mutually exclusive, i.e. no predicate is subsumed by any other predicate.
the number of topological predicate groups is finite and can be reduced from 2,048 to 1,280 by using the concepts of topologically clustered and grouped topological predicates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of topological predicates for complex spatial objects is much larger than the number of topologically meaningful predicates for simple spatial objects.
the design of a suitable query language for complex spatial data types requires a careful consideration of the topological relationships between complex objects.
topological relationships are applicable to complex spatial objects, and that their number can be significantly reduced.
